answer: Each identity fences one knoll plot running to a lagoon shore and locks a 75-credit bond. The fence uses timber posts with key-signed serial tags in a post log. An auditor walks a random stretch and matches posts to the log; a gap, copied serial, or shared stretch shows as a break. First post costs 29; the kth costs 29+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7022 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,525,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-fence ring fails: serials bind one post to one plot, so a walked stretch exposes reused posts. An honest keeper pays 29 once and recovers the bond on audit.
